# 12 — Tier-D god-class decomposition plan

## Headline finding: the "god-class" is one logical class sprawled across 6 files

`RynthAiPlugin` is declared `public sealed partial class` and physically split across **6 files totalling 8,312 lines** (verified: `grep -rl 'partial class RynthAiPlugin'`). The prior audit's **~6,036** figure ≈ the **5 plumbing partials = 6,018 lines** (everything *except* the `CorpseOpenController` looting FSM). The 6th partial, `CorpseOpenController.cs` (2,294), is genuine subsystem logic wearing the plugin's clothes.

| Partial file | Lines | ImGui | Host. | Nature | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| `RynthAiPlugin.cs` | 2,276 | 3 | 108 | lifecycle · wiring · tick-arbiter · event routing · telemetry · config-glue | REFACTOR → kernel |
| `RynthAiCommands.cs` | 2,614 | 0 | 86 | `/ra` chat-command dispatch (~55 handlers) | REFACTOR (headless-relevant, but string-parsed) |
| `MagToolsCommands.cs` | 755 | 0 | 48 | `/mt` MagTools-compat command dispatch | REFACTOR |
| `DoorInteractionController.cs` | 310 | 0 | — | door-open FSM (partial of plugin) | KEEP-HEADLESS (extract) |
| `UtilityBeltCommands.cs` | 63 | 0 | — | utility-belt command shims | DELETE/fold |
| `CorpseOpenController.cs` | 2,294 | 0 | 53 | corpse-loot FSM (partial of plugin) | KEEP-HEADLESS (extract) |
| **Σ plumbing (5, ex-corpse)** | **6,018** | | | **≈ the audited 6,036** | |

A **second** god-class sits beside it: `LegacyUi/LegacyDashboardRenderer.cs` (2,965 lines, **193 ImGui calls, 0 Host calls**). It is *not* a partial of the plugin — it is a separate `internal sealed class` (`LegacyDashboardRenderer.cs:15`) — but it is triple-duty and **owns the config object every subsystem depends on**, so it cannot be deleted wholesale.

## (b) Extraction plan — the minimal `BotKernel`

Everything the plugin plumbing does resolves to **five kernel duties**. Extract these ~1,200 lines of *logic* (out of the 6,018 lines of *plumbing*) and the ImGui/host-HUD/ABI scaffolding falls away.

| Kernel duty | Replaces (today) | Web-port note |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Config + blackboard** `BotConfig` | `LegacyUiSettings` + `LegacyDashboardRenderer` load/save/profile (`:217–366,1101,1171`) | POCO already (`LegacyUiSettings.cs` has **0 ImGui**; blackboard fields `IsMacroRunning :21`, `CurrentState :23`, `BotAction :26`). Persistence → localStorage/IndexedDB or JSON over the wsbridge. |
| **2. Construction/wiring** `BuildSession()` | `OnLoginComplete` (`:253–426`) — 21 `new X` + cross-wires, strict order (Buff before Combat, then back-wire `:382`) | Straight lift; feed subsystems `(host-shim, config, objectCache)` instead of `_dashboard.Settings`. |
| **3. Tick routing** `Tick()` | `OnTick` arbiter ladder (`:1083–1395`) + `ActivityArbiter.ApplyStep2` (`:1094`) | Pure logic. Call from a JS `rAF`/`netDrainHz` pump instead of host `TickAll`. Drop HUD-suppression `:911–921` and `SubmitNav3D :1410`. |
| **4. Event ingest** `Dispatch(evt)` | `On{CreateObject,DeleteObject,UpdateHealth,ChatWindowText,KillNotification,…}` (`:1471–1552`) | Convert synchronous host callbacks → messages drained from the session state machine (the poll-vs-async inversion). `OnChatWindowText :1471` fans to 8 subsystems — becomes an event-bus subscribe. |
| **5. Lifecycle** `Init/Teardown` | `Initialize :138`, `TeardownSession :214`, in-world gate `:996–1024` | Keep as-is; `GetPlayerId==0` debounce maps to session-disconnect. |

**Subsystems liftable *unmodified* once the kernel exists** — all 13 already take a `RynthCoreHost` + `LegacyUiSettings` and nothing UI-side (verified via ctor grep):

|---|---|---|

| `MetaManager`(+ExpressionEngine) | `MetaManager.cs:85` | 1,220 (+3,738) |
| `NavigationEngine` | `NavigationEngine.cs:137` | 1,564 |

Plus, once promoted out of the partial: **`CorpseOpenController` (2,294) and `DoorInteractionController` (310)** — currently partials, but their bodies only touch `host`/`objectCache`/`combatManager`/`config`, so they lift with a ctor signature change.

**Deleted, not ported:** `OnRender`+ImGui resolver (`:2201–2276`), retail-HUD suppression (`:911–921`), Nav3D submit (`:1410`), `LegacyDashboardRenderer` render half (~1,500 lines of the 2,965), `UtilityBeltCommands.cs`. **Re-implemented as thin adapters:** the `/ra`+`/mt` command dispatchers (5,229 lines of `RynthAiCommands`+`MagToolsCommands`) become a `Command(string)` → kernel-method map — a web bot calls kernel methods directly, so most handler bodies survive but the string-parsing shell is optional.

## (c) The 3 nastiest entanglements

### 1. The config object AND the runtime arbitration lock live inside the ImGui class
`LegacyUiSettings _settings` is a **private field of `LegacyDashboardRenderer`** (`LegacyDashboardRenderer.cs:33`), surfaced only through the `Settings` getter (`:34`). **13 subsystems are constructed with `_dashboard.Settings`** (`OnLoginComplete`: nav `:262`, spell `:335`, buff `:345`, combat `:373`, missile `:384`, meta `:395`, inventory/mana/pet `:409–411`, salvage `:414`, jumper `:423`). Worse, the tick-arbiter's live lock — `BotAction`/`IsMacroRunning`/`CurrentState` (`LegacyUiSettings.cs:26,21,23`) — is on that same UI-owned object and is written every tick (`OnTick :1106,1260,1269,1307`). All persistence (load/save/profile-switch/char-folder) is also in the renderer (`:217,314,366,1101,187`).
**Cut:** lift `LegacyUiSettings` + its load/save/profile methods into a kernel-owned `BotConfig`/`Blackboard`; the UI (if any) takes a *reference* to it, inverting today's ownership. This is the single highest-leverage cut — it unblocks all 13 unmodified lifts and is why the renderer can't simply be deleted.

### 2. `OnTick` fuses the portable priority-brain with host-HUD pushes and render submit
`RynthAiPlugin.cs:874–1418` is one 544-line method. The valuable, portable core is the arbiter ladder (`:1083–1395`) — but it is interleaved with three non-portable concerns: retail radar/powerbar/FPS suppression writes (`:911–921`, meaningless on web), UI telemetry-feed pushes (`:1186–1225` via `_dashboard?.SetFreeSlots/SetScanCounts/SetEquipment/…`), and a `finally` that submits Nav3D **render** geometry (`:1409–1410`). Because these share the method body and the early-`return` control flow (Buffing `:1152`, crafting `:1287`, boost-nav `:1316`), you cannot lift the brain without dragging the HUD code.
**Cut:** hoist the ladder into `BotKernel.Tick()`; replace `:911–921` with nothing (web has no retail HUD), route `:1186–1225` through an injected `IStatusSink` (no-op on a pure bot, JSON-over-wsbridge for a monitored one), and move `SubmitNav3D` behind an `IRenderHook` that is null on web.

### 3. Two subsystem FSMs are `partial class RynthAiPlugin`, so they have zero interface boundary
`CorpseOpenController.cs` is a complete corpse-loot state machine — private maps `_completedCorpses`, `_processedCorpseItems`, `_corpseItemAttempts`, `_corpseCooldownUntil`, `_corpseAbandonCounts` (`:29–39`) — yet it is declared `partial class RynthAiPlugin` (`:11`). OnTick calls its members as if they were the plugin's own (`TickCorpseOpening() :1321,1329`, `IsCorpseNavigationClaimActive() :1322,1339`, fields `_openedContainerId`/`_targetCorpseId` `:1088,1172,1258`). Being a partial, it reaches straight into `_combatManager`, `_navigationEngine`, `_objectCache` with no seam. `DoorInteractionController.cs` (`TickDoorInteraction() :1312,1389`) has the same shape. This is what inflates the "god-class" line count: 2,604 lines of liftable subsystem are *syntactically* fused into the plugin.
**Cut:** promote both to standalone classes — `CorpseLooter(host, config, objectCache, nav, combat)` and `DoorController(host, config, nav)` — replacing partial-field access with ctor-injected refs. The kernel then owns them like any other subsystem, and the plumbing shrinks from 6,018 to ~3,400 lines.
